name: Account for investment transactions and income daily (one business day's cycle)
summary: Each business day the fund's accounting book of record, SimCorp Dimension, posts the day's trades, income accruals, FX revaluation, derivative and collateral entries and the private investment cash flows that other systems send it. The next morning fund accountants check that the batch and interfaces are complete, clear the exception queue and suspense accounts, review income, FX, derivative, private and treasury postings, prepare manual journals for flows the systems could not post, and tie the ledger to the positions and cash that reconciliation has agreed with the custodian. A senior associate approves manual journals and signs off the day's ledger, which is then posted to the corporate general ledger. Late private investment data, missing reference data and waiting for the custodian reconciliation are the usual reasons the day slips.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund investment manager that invests one fund globally with mostly internal teams, keeps its investment accounting in-house on SimCorp Dimension and reports under IFRS as an investment entity.
baseline.notes: The case is the whole fund's daily accounting cycle, from the end of trading day T to the sign-off of that day's ledger, usually during T+1.

unit_of_work: one business day's investment accounting cycle
trigger: The trading day closes and SimCorp starts its overnight accounting batch for that day.
end_state: The day's investment ledger is signed off by a senior associate, posted to the corporate general ledger and locked.

volume.seasonality: Heavier on quarter-end and month-end days and in the April to June dividend season; the process runs every Toronto business day.

evidence.note: One cycle per Toronto business day, as in the organisation file's process map.

Daily accounting duties match the model fund investment accounting postings. Title and loaded cost from the organisation file. Touch minutes in this file are the person-minutes of the reviewers on the critical path; many accountants work the same steps in parallel by portfolio and asset class, so fte_on_process is set above the FTE implied by touch time. The other accountants of the 45 work on month-end, financial statements, holding subsidiaries' statutory accounts and audit.

Seniors review exceptions, approve manual journals and sign off the daily ledger. Title and loaded cost from the organisation file. Touch minutes in this file are the person-minutes of the reviewers on the critical path; many accountants work the same steps in parallel by portfolio and asset class, so fte_on_process is set above the FTE implied by touch time.

roles.title: Director, fund accounting and financial reporting

evidence.note: Weekly review of aged suspense and approval of large manual journals. Title and loaded cost from the organisation file. Touch minutes in this file are the person-minutes of the reviewers on the critical path; many accountants work the same steps in parallel by portfolio and asset class, so fte_on_process is set above the FTE implied by touch time.

systems.name: SimCorp Dimension investment book of record (portfolio accounting, treasury, performance)
Private investments administration and cash flow system
Corporate ERP (general ledger, accounts payable, budgeting)
Global custodian web portal and statements
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
Cloud enterprise data platform and data warehouse

steps.name: Run the overnight accounting batch
steps.description: After the day's trading cut-off, SimCorp runs its overnight jobs: it posts the day's trades on trade date, accrues interest and dividends, revalues foreign currency balances at the day's FX rates, marks positions to the loaded prices and generates the accounting entries and sub-ledger balances.

error.defect_description: A job fails or runs on incomplete prices or rates.

evidence.note: Trade date recording, FX translation and accruals from the accounting policies; SimCorp as the portfolio accounting system. Batch timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Load interface postings from other systems
steps.description: Interfaces bring in entries from the private investments administration system (capital calls, distributions, fees, closings), the collateral system (margin and collateral), treasury activity and plan transfers. Validation rules park any entry with an unknown account, security or transaction type in a suspense account and an exception queue.

error.defect_description: An interface file is loaded twice or partly.

evidence.note: Connectivity between the accounting book of record, custodians and the ledger; suspense routing is the author's description of common configuration.

steps.name: Check batch completion and interface control totals
steps.description: First thing in the morning an accountant checks that every overnight job finished, and compares record counts and amount totals of each interface with the sending system's control report. Missing prices or FX rates and incomplete loads are flagged before anyone reviews balances.

error.defect_description: A partial load is missed.

control.basis: Completeness and accuracy controls over interfaces and batch processing within internal control over financial reporting (COSO 2013), certified by the CEO and CFRO and audited by the external auditor

evidence.note: ICFR certification and audit from the annual report; pre-close readiness checks from FundCount. Minutes and failure rate are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Raise an incident for a failed job or interface
steps.description: The accountant logs a ticket with the technology support team, describing the failed job or file and its business impact, and agrees whether to rerun it or wait for a corrected file from the source system.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Rerun the failed job or interface
steps.description: Technology support fixes the cause or obtains a corrected file and reruns the job, and SimCorp regenerates the affected entries.

error.defect_description: Rerun creates duplicate entries.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the wait depends on technology support availability.

steps.name: Work the exception queue and clear suspense
steps.description: Accountants open the exception queue and suspense accounts, identify each parked entry, and fix the account mapping, transaction type or portfolio, or write down what reference data is missing. Items left in suspense are listed with their age.

error.defect_description: An entry is cleared to the wrong account or portfolio.

evidence.note: Exception handling of transactions in the posting; suspense should not age beyond one close cycle. Minutes are the author's estimate of team effort on the critical path.

steps.name: Request a reference data fix
steps.description: The accountant emails or tickets investment data management with the security or account that is missing or wrong in the security master, for example a new bond with no coupon schedule or a swap with the wrong currency, and asks for the fix.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; reference data comes from the organisation's data management process.

steps.name: Reprocess suspended entries after the data fix
steps.description: Once data management corrects the security master, SimCorp reprocesses the suspended transactions and accruals and moves them out of suspense.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of data team turnaround.

steps.name: Review income accruals and corporate action postings
steps.description: Accountants compare the day's dividend, coupon and withholding tax postings with the corporate actions calendar and the custodian's income reports, check that dividends were accrued on ex-date and that large accrual movements make sense.

error.defect_description: A wrong rate or missed ex-date passes review.

evidence.note: Dividends recognised at ex-date; corporate actions named as a common breakpoint. Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review FX rates and revaluation postings
steps.description: An accountant checks that the day's closing FX rates loaded from the single approved source, that revaluation of foreign currency balances and unsettled forwards posted, and that large FX gains or losses match the day's currency moves.

error.defect_description: A wrong or stale rate passes review.

evidence.note: FX translation policy; one FX source across ledger and reports; revaluation entries tie to sub-ledgers.

steps.name: Review derivative, financing and collateral postings
steps.description: Accountants check futures variation margin, swap resets and accruals, option premiums, repo and securities lending entries, and the collateral postings from the collateral system, and tie cash margin to the day's margin summary.

error.defect_description: A margin or reset posting is missed or doubled.

evidence.note: Repo, securities lending and collateral accounting policies in the annual report; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review private investment cash flows
steps.description: Accountants check capital calls, distributions, manager fees and closing payments posted from the private investments system against the cash that moved at the custodian, and look for flows that are known but not yet booked because notices or allocations arrived late.

error.defect_description: A distribution is split wrongly between income and return of capital.

next.condition: late or incomplete private data needs a manual journal

evidence.note: Cash flow reconciliations in the posting; capital activity misalignment as a breakpoint. The 35% share of days needing a manual journal is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare manual journal entries with support
steps.description: For a flow or correction the systems cannot post, the accountant prepares a manual journal in SimCorp with the amounts, accounts and portfolio, attaches the notice, wire confirmation or calculation, and writes a reason code.

error.defect_description: Wrong account, sign or portfolio on the journal.

evidence.note: Adjusting journal entries in the posting; support package and reason code for manual journals.

steps.name: Review and approve manual journals
steps.description: A senior associate checks each manual journal against its support, confirms the accounts and amounts, and approves it in SimCorp or sends it back. The preparer cannot approve their own journal.

error.defect_description: Approver misses an error.

control.basis: Independent review and approval of manual journal entries with support under internal control over financial reporting (COSO 2013)

evidence.note: Preparer and approver on material journals and separation of preparation from approval; ICFR framework from the annual report.

steps.name: Check treasury, plan transfer and account allocation postings
steps.description: An accountant checks term debt, commercial paper and financing entries, any plan transfer in or out that day, and that income, expenses and transfers are split correctly between the base plan and additional plan accounts.

error.defect_description: Allocation between the two accounts is wrong.

evidence.note: Weekly plan transfers, at least monthly returns of funds, and separate base and additional plan accounts in the annual report.

steps.name: Tie the accounting ledger to the reconciled positions and cash
steps.description: Once reconciliation has signed off the custodian reconciliation, accountants compare SimCorp accounting positions and cash by account with the reconciled position record and tie sub-ledger balances to the ledger, and list any difference.

error.defect_description: A small difference is written off as rounding.

control.basis: Sub-ledger to ledger and book of record to custodian position and cash reconciliation as key controls over financial reporting (COSO 2013)

evidence.note: Sub-ledger to general ledger reconciliations and NAV and cash flow reconciliations in the posting; unreconciled cash zero or explained. Waiting for the reconciliation sign-off is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Investigate ledger differences with operations
steps.description: The accountant traces each difference to the transaction behind it, asks reconciliation, trade support or private operations what happened, and books or requests the correcting entry.

error.defect_description: Correction booked to the wrong period.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; responses from operations teams set the wait.

steps.name: Record investment holding subsidiary activity
steps.description: Accountants record the day's transactions in the investment holding subsidiaries, such as capital contributions, loans and dividends to the parent, and update the look-through records of their underlying investments. These subsidiaries are carried at fair value rather than consolidated.

error.defect_description: Activity booked in the wrong subsidiary.

evidence.note: Investment holding subsidiaries are not consolidated but measured at fair value based on underlying investments; dividends from them are income. Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run the daily trial balance and movement analytics
steps.description: An accountant runs the daily trial balance and a net asset movement report by portfolio, and compares the change in net assets with market moves, cash flows and transfers to flag unusual items for the senior.

error.defect_description: Unusual movement not flagged.

evidence.note: Analytical review with variance commentary before approval.

steps.name: Investigate an unexplained movement
steps.description: The senior associate looks into the flagged item with the accountant and the investment or operations team, decides whether it is a booking error or a real economic movement, and asks for a correcting journal if needed.

error.defect_description: Real error explained away.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the daily checklist and sign off the ledger
steps.description: The senior associate reviews the completed daily checklist, the open suspense list with ages, the tie-out and the movement commentary, and signs off the day's ledger or sends items back.

error.defect_description: Sign-off with an unexplained suspense item.

control.basis: Daily review and sign-off of investment accounting as a control over financial reporting (COSO 2013, CEO/CFRO certification)

evidence.note: ICFR certification; reconciliation and accrual sign-offs before final approval.

steps.name: Review aged suspense and large manual journals
steps.description: Once a week the director reviews suspense items older than a few days, the log of manual journals and any journal above the senior's limit, asks for clearing dates and approves the large journals.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Management authorities: journal approval limits and monthly suspense ageing review

evidence.note: Management authorities in the internal control framework; suspense should not age beyond one close cycle. Weekly cadence is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Post the day's ledger to the corporate general ledger
steps.description: The approved day's summarised investment entries are interfaced from SimCorp to the corporate ERP general ledger and the day is locked, so month-end close and tax receive final balances.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Connectivity from the accounting book of record to the general ledger; batch timing is the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Failed overnight job or interface
exceptions.description: A batch job or interface fails; the accountant raises an incident and the day waits for the rerun before review can start.

exceptions.name: Missing reference data
exceptions.description: New securities or swaps lack static data, so their entries sit in suspense until data management fixes the security master.

exceptions.name: Late private investment data
exceptions.description: Capital calls, distributions or fees are known from cash movements but not booked by the systems, so accountants post manual journals that a senior approves.

exceptions.name: Ledger does not tie to reconciled positions
exceptions.description: A difference between the accounting ledger and the reconciled position record is traced with operations and corrected.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the end of trading day T to sign-off of that day's ledger
benchmarks.population: Daily investment accounting at large in-house asset owners

evidence.note: No published figure. Author's estimate: the overnight batch finishes before the morning, review and tie-out run through T+1, and sign-off lands on the evening of T+1 or the next morning when private data or the custodian reconciliation is late.

benchmarks.metric: straight-through processing rate claimed for an outsourced investment accounting service
benchmarks.unit: share of transactions processed without manual touch (more than)
benchmarks.population: SimCorp marketing claim for its investment accounting service

evidence.note: Vendor claim of over 95%.

pain_points.description: Private investment cash flows arrive late or without allocation detail, so accountants post and later reverse manual journals.

evidence.note: Capital activity misalignment and unsupported manual journals listed as common breakpoints.

pain_points.description: Missing security master data parks entries in suspense until another team fixes it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

pain_points.description: The ledger tie-out waits for the reconciliation team's sign-off, which itself waits for custodian files and break investigation.

evidence.note: Author's estimate based on the order of the daily processes.

pain_points.description: Investment holding subsidiaries add a second layer of records that must stay consistent with the parent's fair value of each subsidiary.

evidence.note: Holding subsidiaries measured at fair value based on their underlying investments.

sources.title: NAV Oversight: Controls, Review Workflow, and Common Breakpoints
sources.supports: Book cash reconciled to bank or custodian with unreconciled cash zero or fully explained; one FX source across ledger, positions and reports; fee and expense accruals tied to terms; each manual journal needs a support package and reason code, and entries after cutoff need explicit approval; separation of preparation from approval; breakpoints include late trades, FX inconsistency, corporate actions and unsupported manual journals.

sources.supports: Clear clearing and suspense accounts so nothing ages beyond one close cycle; FX revaluation entries tie to sub-ledgers; preparer and approver stamps on material journals and reconciliations; maker-checker enforced.

sources.supports: NOC 11100 hourly wages, Toronto Region: low 25.00, median 41.34, high 74.36 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: The organisation file's process description says holding subsidiaries add consolidation entries; the F2022 annual report says investment holding subsidiaries are not consolidated but carried at fair value as the organisation is an investment entity under IFRS 10. This file models subsidiary bookkeeping and look-through records, not consolidation.

Touch minutes are the person-minutes of the accountants on the critical path for the whole fund. In practice several accountants work steps s09 to s12 in parallel by asset class; the simulator adds them in sequence, so its cycle time is longer than the elapsed time of a normal day.

fte_on_process (about 9 FTE) is set near the top of the validator's range because many accountants spend part of each day on these steps; the organisation file gives 45 accountants, 25 seniors and 4 directors in fund accounting and financial reporting, who also run month-end close, financial statements and audit.
Branch probabilities (10% failed jobs, 25% days with missing reference data, 35% days with manual private journals, 20% tie-out differences) are the author's estimates.

The annual report says plan transfers arrive weekly, while the organisation file's tf-plan-transfers process has one or two cases a month; this file only checks the postings and does not depend on the count.
Loaded hourly costs are the organisation file's, which include incentive pay and an overhead factor of 1.25; they are far above the Job Bank Toronto median for NOC 11100 of 41.34 an hour (2023-2024).
The simulated median cycle time (about 2.1 days) is above the 1.3-day benchmark estimate mainly because parallel review steps are added in sequence by the simulator.
